2026-08-17.content:
Support for the Advanced malware sandbox (WildFire) service is now restored.
You can now use Advanced malware sandbox to perform deep inspection of
network-routed file transfers and block zero-day malware before it reaches
your workloads. Advanced malware sandbox
is available in the Cloud Next Generation Firewall Enterprise tier.

For more information, see
[Advanced malware sandbox overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/about-wildfire) and
[Configure Advanced malware sandbox in your network](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/configure-wildfire).
This feature is available in **Preview**.

summary.title: Advanced malware sandbox support restored
summary.summary: Support for the Advanced malware sandbox service has been restored, allowing for deep inspection of file transfers and blocking of zero-day malware. This feature is available in the Cloud Next Generation Firewall Enterprise tier and is currently in Preview.

2026-07-30.content:
The limits for the following Cloud NGFW resources have been updated:

* Security profile groups with threat prevention per project: 35
* Security profile groups with URL filtering per project: 35
* Firewall endpoint associations per organization-level firewall endpoint: 50
* Firewall endpoint associations per project-level firewall endpoint: 50

For more information, see [Quotas and limits](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/quotas).

summary.title: Cloud NGFW resource limits updated
summary.summary: The limits for several Cloud NGFW resources have been increased. This includes security profile groups for threat prevention and URL filtering, as well as firewall endpoint associations. For detailed information, please refer to the updated quotas and limits documentation.

2026-07-27.content:
Enabling Advanced malware sandbox (WildFire) in an existing firewall
endpoint can cause a temporary data plane outage. As a result, the
Advanced malware sandbox feature is temporarily removed.

summary.title: Malware Sandbox Feature Temporarily Removed
summary.summary: Enabling the Advanced malware sandbox feature in an existing firewall endpoint may cause a temporary data plane outage. Consequently, the Advanced malware sandbox feature has been temporarily removed.

2026-07-20.content:
You can now use the Advanced malware sandbox (WildFire) service to protect
your network against unknown, novel malware, and file-based threats.
Advanced malware sandbox integrates dynamic machine learning (ML) and
cloud-based behavioral sandboxing to perform deep inspection of network-routed
file transfers and block zero-day malware before it reaches your workloads.
Advanced malware sandbox is available in the Cloud Firewall Enterprise tier.

For more information, see [Advanced malware sandbox overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/about-wildfire) and
[Configure Advanced malware sandbox in your network](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/configure-wildfire). This
feature is available in **Preview**.

summary.title: Protect Against Unknown Malware
summary.summary: The new Advanced malware sandbox service now protects your network from unknown and novel malware. It uses machine learning and cloud-based behavioral sandboxing to inspect file transfers and block zero-day threats before they impact your workloads. This feature is available in the Cloud Firewall Enterprise tier and is currently in Preview.

2026-06-30.content:
You can now create and configure project-level resources for application layer
inspection in Cloud NGFW, including project-level firewall endpoints, security
profile groups, and security profiles. For more information, see
[Organization-level and project-level
resources](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/about-app-layer-inspection#org-project-resources),
[Firewall endpoints overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/about-firewall-endpoints),
[Security profile groups overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/about-security-profile-groups),
and [Security profiles overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/about-security-profiles). This
feature is available in **General Availability**.

summary.title: Application Layer Inspection for Projects
summary.summary: Project-level resources for application layer inspection are now available in general availability. You can create and configure firewall endpoints, security profile groups, and security profiles at the project level. This enhances your network security capabilities within your projects.

2026-06-30.content:
To restrict traffic to the managed Envoy proxies in a
[proxy-only subnet](https://docs.cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/proxy-only-subnets), you can configure
global network firewall policies and regional network firewall policies to
protect internal Application Load Balancers and internal proxy Network Load
Balancers. For more information, see [Use global network firewall policies to
protect Envoy-based load balancers](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/global-network-app-lb) and
[Use regional network firewall policies to protect internal Application Load
Balancers and internal proxy Network Load
Balancers](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/regional-network-app-lb). This feature is available in
**General Availability**.

summary.title: New Firewall Policies for Load Balancers
summary.summary: You can now use global and regional network firewall policies to protect internal Application Load Balancers and internal proxy Network Load Balancers. This feature helps restrict traffic to managed Envoy proxies within your proxy-only subnets. It is now available in General Availability.

2026-05-04.content:
You can now create and configure the following organization-level Cloud NGFW
resources within a Google Cloud project:

* Security profiles
* Security profile groups
* Firewall endpoints
* Firewall endpoint associations

For more information, see [Security profile
overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/about-security-profiles), [Security profile group
overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/about-security-profile-groups), and [Firewall endpoint
overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/about-firewall-endpoints). This feature is available in **Public preview**.

summary.title: Manage Cloud NGFW resources in projects
summary.summary: You can now create and configure organization-level Cloud NGFW resources, including security profiles, security profile groups, firewall endpoints, and firewall endpoint associations, directly within a Google Cloud project. This feature is currently in Public preview.

2026-03-24.content:
You can use the URL filtering service to filter your workload traffic by using
domain and Server Name Indication (SNI) information available in the egress
HTTP(S) messages. For more information, see
[URL filtering service overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/about-url-filtering). This
feature is available in **General Availability**.

summary.title: Filter network traffic using URL filtering
summary.summary: You can now filter your workload traffic by using domain and Server Name Indication (SNI) information in egress HTTP(S) messages. This feature is now generally available.

2026-03-23.content:
Secure tags with a `purpose-data` attribute specifying a VPC network or an
organization now support VPC networks that are connected using VPC Network
Peering. For more information, see
[Secure tags for firewalls](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/tags-firewalls-overview).
This feature is available in **General Availability**.

summary.title: Secure tags now support VPC Network Peering
summary.summary: Secure tags with a purpose-data attribute now support VPC networks connected using VPC Network Peering. This enhancement allows for more flexible and secure network configurations. This feature is now generally available.

2026-02-25.content:
You can use network contexts to meet your security goals by using fewer
firewall policy rules more efficiently. For more information, see
[Network contexts](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/understand-network-contexts). This feature
is available in **General Availability**.

summary.title: Use network contexts for efficient firewall policies
summary.summary: Network contexts allow you to achieve your security goals with fewer, more efficient firewall policy rules. This feature is now in General Availability, enabling simpler and more effective network security management.

2026-02-19.content:
Cloud NGFW now supports regional system firewall policies. Regional system
firewall policies are read-only policies that internal Google services, such as
Google Kubernetes Engine, use to secure their operations within a VPC network.
For more information, see [Regional system firewall
policies](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/firewall-policies-overview#regional-system-firewall-policies).
This feature is available in **General Availability**.

summary.title: New Regional System Firewall Policies
summary.summary: Cloud NGFW now supports regional system firewall policies, which are read-only policies used by internal Google services like GKE to secure operations within a VPC network. This feature is now generally available.

2026-01-13.content: You can now create regional firewall policies that apply to managed Envoy proxies used by internal Application Load Balancers and internal proxy Network Load Balancers. For more information, see [Use regional network firewall policies to protect internal Application Load Balancers and internal proxy Network Load Balancers](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/regional-network-app-lb). This feature is available in **Preview**.

summary.title: Regional firewall policies for internal load balancers
summary.summary: You can now create regional firewall policies for internal Application Load Balancers and internal proxy Network Load Balancers. This feature is available in Preview.

2025-11-17.content: You can create a Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) over converged ethernet (RoCE) Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) network and configure firewall rules that apply to the network. For more information, see [Cloud NGFW for RoCE VPC networks](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/firewall-for-roce). This feature is available in **General Availability**.

summary.title: RDMA over Converged Ethernet (RoCE) Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) now in General Availability
summary.summary: You can now create a Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) over Converged Ethernet (RoCE) Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) network and configure firewall rules for it. This feature is now in General Availability.

2025-11-13.content: You can create a firewall endpoint that supports jumbo frames up to 8,500 bytes in size. For more information, see [Supported packet size](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/about-firewall-endpoints#supported-packet-size). This feature is available in **General Availability**.

summary.title: Firewall endpoints now support jumbo frames
summary.summary: You can now create firewall endpoints that support jumbo frames up to 8,500 bytes. This feature is in General Availability.

2025-09-23.content: You can use the URL filtering service to filter your workload traffic by using domain and Server Name Indication (SNI) information available in the egress HTTP(S) messages. For more information, see [URL filtering service overview](https://cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/about-url-filtering). This feature is available in **Preview**.

summary.title: URL filtering for workload traffic
summary.summary: Filter your workload traffic using domain and SNI information from HTTP(S) messages. This feature is available in Preview.

2025-08-04.content: You can create a secure tag at the organization level and bind its value to all virtual machine (VM) instances across that organization. For more information, see [Secure tags for firewalls](https://cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/tags-firewalls-overview). This feature is available in **General Availability**.

summary.title: Organization-level secure tags
summary.summary: Securely tag all VM instances across your organization.

2025-07-25.content: You can create a Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) over converged ethernet (RoCE) Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) network and configure firewall rules that apply to the network. For more information, see [Cloud NGFW for RoCE VPC networks](https://cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/firewall-for-roce). This feature is available in **Preview**.

summary.title: RDMA over Converged Ethernet (RoCE) VPC Network Feature
summary.summary: New feature: RDMA over converged ethernet (RoCE) Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) network and firewall rules configuration.

2025-06-23.content: You can create a secure tag at the organization level and bind its value to all virtual machine (VM) instances across that organization, instead of applying tags to instances within a specific network. For more information, see [Secure tags for firewalls](https://cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/tags-firewalls-overview). This feature is available in **Preview**.

summary.title: Organization-Level Secure Tags Now Available
summary.summary: You can now create secure tags at the organization level, applying them to all virtual machine instances organization-wide. This simplifies tag management and enhances security across your infrastructure. The feature is currently in Preview.
